rationale.conceptual: The paper uses a custom multi-component method: self-consistent LDA slab calculations with a controlled excess charge, subsequent Stark-shift determination (via dipole moment or bulk-feature alignment), and identification of surface states from minima in the Δn difference curves. These steps go beyond black-box DFT and require a genuine understanding of charged-slab electrostatics, energy alignment, and DOS analysis, plus translating the formal equations into a practical workflow.
rationale.execution: The pipeline comprises 7 distinct stages: bulk Ca reference, neutral 5-layer slab, two separate charged-slab runs (q=0.01, q=0.03), work-function extraction, DOS peak-shift computation, and extraction of occupied and unoccupied surface-state energies. The stages are interdependent, involve setting up and converging several DFT calculations, and demand careful data post-processing (alignment, Stark correction, curve analysis), making this a long, multi-tool orchestration with fragile handoffs.

difficulty.reasoning: Reproducing this work requires a multi-step DFT pipeline with a custom charged-slab method for surface-state extraction. Conceptual understanding involves handling electrostatic response, Stark-shift correction, and difference-DOS analysis; the execution demands several interdependent slab calculations and careful data post-processing.

compute_estimate.reasoning: The system is a 5-layer Ca slab with a simple fcc lattice, treated with LDA. The DFT calculations are small and can run on a single CPU core in minutes; the only data are a few pseudopotential files, so resource needs are minimal.
